slides.title: Your cache is serving **old data**. Now what?
4 ways to keep a cache **fresh**
bullets: ⏳|**TTL**: every key expires on its own
🗑️|**Delete on write**: change the DB, drop the key
📣|**Events / CDC**: a change message invalidates keys

slides.title: Pick TTL by your **staleness budget**
slides.text: Seconds for prices, minutes for profiles, hours for static content. Add jitter so keys do not expire together.
slides.code:
SET user:42 "<json>" EX 300
TTL user:42      → seconds left
PERSIST user:42  → remove TTL

cols.title: 😴 Lazy
cols.text: Checks the TTL when a key is accessed.

cols.title: 🔄 Active
cols.text: Samples ~20 keys with TTLs, several times a second. Repeats if over 25% expired.

slides.title: Now **eviction** kicks in
slides.text: Default is `noeviction`: writes fail, reads still work.

slides.title: Pick your **eviction policy**
bullets: ⏱️|`volatile-*`: only keys that have a TTL

slides.title: **Recent** or **popular**?

cols.title: 🕰️ LRU
cols.text: Keeps recent keys. One big scan can wash out hot keys.

cols.title: 📊 LFU
cols.text: Keeps popular keys. Slow to forget, so counters decay.

slides.text: Redis samples a few keys (default 5), it does not track exact LRU.

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: **TTL + delete on write** keep data fresh, with **jitter** to avoid mass expiry. When memory is full, a cache uses **allkeys-lru** or **allkeys-lfu**. LRU favours **recency**, LFU favours **frequency**.
